mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (p > 0.05) despite the FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting stronger labor market confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during prior months with similar labor growth (<50,000).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 850K units for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating robust consumer demand supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in the two months following the demand threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return, as weak manufacturing output signals economic weakness and equity sell-off risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior month's average during INDPRO declines ≥2%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months create a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as disinflation and rate easing reduce policy uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases for 3 months AND FEDFUNDS decreases for 3 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive when both proxies move in opposite directions or only one declines.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 6%, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive due to improved labor market conditions and investor optimism.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the prior month when UNRATE was ≥6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 2% over the next quarter is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting robust economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥2% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the quarter are not significantly higher than during prior quarters with similar GDP growth (<2%).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales of financial assets) falls by more than 10% in a month, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative, indicating risk-off sentiment from declining investment activity.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than average during months with RSAFS declines ≤10%.
